description: We are two brothers from different cities in Chile! The oldest one is a physician and the youngest one is a software engineer. We will use our knowledge to build PATCH a conceptual healthcare support solution designed to assist astronauts during medical emergencies in space, addressing the challenges of limited medical resources, remote environments, and communication delays with Earth.
summary:
We developed PATCH, an onboard medical assessment prototype for astronauts who may need to respond to a health concern before a flight surgeon on Earth can reply. PATCH addresses the astronaut health monitoring challenge by guiding crews through safety checks, symptom reporting, vital signs, and available examination findings.

The prototype replays four recorded MedGemma interviews. In the palpitations scenario, a crew member suddenly feels faint, so PATCH pauses the interview and requires a fresh check of responsiveness and breathing. The crew can then document the findings available and prepare a structured handoff. The demo simulates the delay before that message reaches Earth.

PATCH gives the crew a clear next step during the wait and gives the flight surgeon a record of what happened, what was observed, and what remains unknown.
details:
PATCH focuses on the first few minutes of an onboard medical assessment, when a crew member needs to gather information and ground support may be delayed. The crew begins by recording whether the person is responsive and breathing normally. Both findings must be confirmed before the interview starts. An unknown answer keeps the check pending, and a negative answer brings up predefined emergency guidance based on the recorded findings.

The prototype includes four fictional cases: abdominal pain, left flank pain, lightheadedness and weakness, and palpitations. Each case replays a recorded interview and saves reported observations as the crew proceeds. In the palpitations case, the patient reports feeling faint. PATCH pauses the routine interview and requires a new safety check. If both findings are confirmed, the crew can send a partial handoff using the information collected up to that point.

PATCH organizes the handoff using SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) and shows its delivery after a simulated 15-minute one-way delay. We built the interface in Python with Streamlit and use SQLite to retain assessments and message records locally. Our goal is to make it easier for crews to document changing symptoms and give flight surgeons a useful record to review when contact is delayed.
